short: Sixty-one years on the throne, the longest reign in Chinese history.
full:
He became emperor in February 1661 at the age of seven, four regents governing in his name, and took power himself in 1669 by having the dominant one, Oboi, arrested at an audience. The Manchu conquest was still unfinished. Between 1673 and 1681 he put down the Revolt of the Three Feudatories, the rising of the Chinese generals who had been granted the south, and in 1683 his navy took Taiwan from the last Ming loyalist regime, bringing the island under mainland rule for the first time.

He fought the Dzungar leader Galdan in Mongolia in person, and settled the northern border with Russia by the Treaty of Nerchinsk in 1689, negotiated in Latin through Jesuit interpreters. Those Jesuits worked at his court as astronomers and cartographers until the papacy's ruling against Chinese ancestral rites soured the relationship. In 1712 he fixed the head-tax quota permanently, in effect ending taxation of population growth. He sponsored the Kangxi Dictionary and died on 20 December 1722 after a long, bitter contest among his sons.
